public_rationale: The November 21 settlement secured Altman's return and a replacement board two days after the forecast. OpenAI confirmed implementation on November 29. This satisfies the contextual meaning of a quick stakeholder victory. D'Angelo remained, so the result was displacement of the opposing majority, not every director. It does not establish permanent investor control or abandonment of the nonprofit mission.
limitations: Marcus supplied no exact deadline for 'quickly'.
The settlement was announced within two days; formal confirmation followed ten days after the post.
The hedged claim that victory had already happened on November 19 is not separately established.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: All signs are that OpenAI's financially interested stakeholders (employees and investors) will quickly win out over the nonprofit board, and arguably they already have.

statement.excerpt: All signs are that those financially-interested stakeholders will quickly emerge victorious. (Arguably, they already have).
statement.document_title: “No one person should be trusted here.”

our_interpretation: In context, victory means securing Altman's return and displacing the board majority that removed him.
'Quickly' means resolution within days during the immediate leadership dispute. It does not supply a fixed calendar deadline.
'All signs are' expresses confidence and 'arguably' qualifies the aside about prior success; neither is an external condition that must occur before scoring.
Victory does not require removal of every director, unlimited investor control, or proof that the nonprofit mission was abandoned.
criteria.support_condition: The immediate dispute ends with Altman's return and replacement of the opposing board majority.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive settlement of the immediate dispute retains Altman's dismissal and the opposing board's control, defeating the stakeholders' stated objectives. Mere delay without such a settlement is insufficient.
